Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott

Class OttSecondFactorFilter

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.web.filter.GenericFilterBean
org.springframework.security.web.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationProcessingFilter
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott.OttSecondFactorFilter
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.servlet.Filter, org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanNameAware, org.springframework.beans.factory.DisposableBean, org.springframework.beans.factory.InitializingBean, org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware, org.springframework.context.EnvironmentAware, org.springframework.context.MessageSourceAware, org.springframework.core.env.EnvironmentCapable, org.springframework.web.context.ServletContextAware
public class OttSecondFactorFilter extends org.springframework.security.web.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationProcessingFilter
Processes the post of the one-time code form of the second factor (POST /login/second-factor/ott), in the way TotpAuthenticationFilter processes the TOTP forms. The code is verified by OttSecondFactorAuthenticationProvider against the binding id the session holds; on success the session id is changed (and the CSRF token renewed, with the session authentication strategy of the chain, as the form login does), the enriched authentication is saved to the session and the browser resumes the request that was interrupted. On failure it goes back to the page where the code is typed with ?error. Only a user who has already presented a primary factor may post. The endpoint is owned by this filter, like POST /login, so it is not part of the pages contract.
